title: Universal Robots Unveils Gen 7, a New Platform for Industrial Automation and Physical AI Deployment
summary: Universal Robots announced Gen 7, a redesigned industrial robot platform built to make AI deployment easier on factory floors rather than just in lab demos. The platform has been rebuilt from controller to tool flange with modern software tooling and stronger connectivity, positioning it as an “AI-ready” base for companies trying to integrate physical AI into real automation workflows.

extra.full_text: Redesigned from controller to tool flange, the new Gen 7 robot platform is out-of-the-box AI-ready, giving companies the modern software tools and next-level connectivity that they need to confidently take AI from the lab into industrial operations.

title: 유니버설로봇, 협동로봇 신세대 플랫폼 '젠 7' 공개
summary: Universal Robots unveiled its seventh-generation collaborative robot platform, Gen 7, at IMTS 2026 in Chicago. Built around the PolyScope X robot operating system, the platform redesigns core interaction points including the control box, teach pendant, and tool flange to make setup and demanding industrial tasks easier, with an AI-ready tool flange pointing toward more adaptable cobot deployments.

summary: Elaine Short has begun a sabbatical at Hello Robot working with Stretch, focusing on how in-home robots can better support people with mobility disabilities in everyday household tasks. The devlog frames the effort as both personal and technical: using real home needs to guide progress toward practical assistive robotics rather than lab-only demonstrations.

title: BD Advances Intelligent Robotics to Transform the Future of Pharmacy Care at Fairview
summary: BD has deployed its Vmax 160 pharmacy automation system at Fairview in what it says is the first U.S. installation of this kind, extending robotic pharmacy workflows beyond conventional dispensing. The system is aimed at helping health systems handle rising volumes of specialty therapies, refrigerated drugs, and more complex fulfillment requirements, where manual pharmacy operations are increasingly strained.

summary: University of Tokyo spinout Highlanders has unveiled HLQ EDGE, an industrial quadruped robot built for heavier field work, with a 60 kg payload, up to 330 Nm joint torque, and three hours of continuous operation. Its expansion rail can carry options such as the company’s own robot arm, pointing toward practical deployments in heavy material transport, inspection patrols, and remote manipulation at industrial sites.

title: 국립부경대 김대석 교수팀, 고출력 인공근육 개발…소프트 로봇 분야 활용 기대
summary: Researchers at Pukyong National University led by Prof. Kim Dae-seok developed a higher-power liquid crystal elastomer artificial muscle by redesigning the molecular crosslinking points with a mesogen-mimetic anisotropic crosslinker that resembles the rod-like liquid crystal mesogens in the polymer backbone. The approach targets a key weakness of conventional LCE muscles, mechanical softening at high temperature, so the material can retain stronger force output under heat and may be better suited for soft-robotic actuators.

title: Ask the Experts: Inside Nemotron Post-Training | Nemotron Labs
summary: NVIDIA researchers are hosting a Nemotron Labs session explaining how they produced the final Nemotron model checkpoints through post-training, with a focus on improving intelligence and agentic behavior. The session walks through their pipeline using NeMo Data Designer for task-specific synthetic datasets, NeMo Gym for training environments, and NeMo RL for reinforcement learning, while pointing researchers to open Hugging Face datasets plus Nemotron GitHub recipes and weights they can reuse.

extra.full_text: In this Ask the Experts session, NVIDIA AI researchers explain how they built the final Nemotron model checkpoints through post-training to enhance model intelligence and enable agentic capabilities. They’ll walk through the tools they used, how they structured the data pipeline, and the open resources available for the community to build on. Learn how NeMo Data Designer was used to create task-specific synthetic datasets, NeMo Gym to build and manage training environments, and NeMo RL for reinforcement learning training. Learn about the post-training datasets published on HuggingFace and the recipes and weights on the Nemotron GitHub that are available under open licenses. What you'll learn: Different stages of post-training pipeline that goes into building SOTA models How NVIDIA NeMo libraries was used to implement and run post-training workflows Which datasets, recipes, and model weights are openly available, and where to find them How to start using NeMo Data Designer, NeMo Gym, and NeMo RL in your own post-training workflows Bring your questions about the Nemotron model training pipeline, NVIDIA’s open post-training tools, or how to get started. The researchers behind Nemotron 3 will answer them live.

title: Hirebotics Expands Cobot Reach and Flexibility with New Line Tracking and Linear Rail Capabilities at IMTS
summary: Hirebotics announced new line-tracking and linear-rail capabilities for its collaborative robot systems at IMTS, extending cobot welding/automation-style workflows to jobs like painting parts as they move and handling larger materials across a longer work envelope. The update matters because it lets manufacturers automate awkward, high-mix tasks without redesigning the production line or forcing operators into a new programming experience.

extra.full_text: Extending capabilities of the collaborative robots to automate the painting of moving parts and handle large, cumbersome materials lets manufacturers accomplish difficult tasks without changing experience or workflows
